### Problem: Minimum ASCII delete sum for two strings {#sec-st-p1-ascii}

::: {.p-statement}
Delete characters from `s1` or `s2` until the two strings are equal. The cost of deleting a character is its ASCII code. Return the minimum cost.

$1 \le n, m \le 1000$. On `sea` and `eat` the answer is 231: delete `s` (115) and `t` (116), and both become `ea`. On `delete` and `leet` the answer is 403, by keeping `let`. Keeping the other LCS `eet` costs more.

Source: [LC 712 · Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings](https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-ascii-delete-sum-for-two-strings/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Equal last letters can be kept for free, because deleting either of them would cost its code and the strings would still need to match. Different last letters force a deletion: pay the code of one of them and solve the remaining prefixes. The empty prefix against a non-empty one pays every remaining code. A 0 on that border would say the letters disappeared for free.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $D[i][j]$ = minimum delete cost to make $s[0..i)$ equal $t[0..j)$.
- **Transition.** Equal last letters: $D[i - 1][j - 1]$. Otherwise $\min(D[i - 1][j] + s[i - 1],\ D[i][j - 1] + t[j - 1])$, with the letters read as codes.
- **Base.** $D[i][0]$ and $D[0][j]$ are prefix sums of the codes. **Answer.** $D[n][m]$.
- **Weight form.** Let $W$ be the heaviest common subsequence. The same deletions cost $(\mathrm{sum}\ s + \mathrm{sum}\ t) - 2W$, because each kept letter is saved twice.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i, j)` pays a prefix sum when one side is empty. Otherwise it keeps two equal last letters or pays the cheaper deletion.
:::

```{python}

#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("ascii", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "231"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-ascii-rec
def ascii_rec(a, b):
    def f(i, j):
        if i == 0:
            return sum(ord(b[k]) for k in range(j))
        if j == 0:
            return sum(ord(a[k]) for k in range(i))
        if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
            return f(i - 1, j - 1)
        return min(f(i - 1, j) + ord(a[i - 1]), f(i, j - 1) + ord(b[j - 1]))
    return f(len(a), len(b))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int asciiRec(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b) {
    if (i == 0) { int s = 0; for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) s += b[k]; return s; }
    if (j == 0) { int s = 0; for (int k = 0; k < i; ++k) s += a[k]; return s; }
    if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) return asciiRec(i - 1, j - 1, a, b);
    return min(asciiRec(i - 1, j, a, b) + a[i - 1], asciiRec(i, j - 1, a, b) + b[j - 1]);
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
The same recurrence, stored on the pair `(i, j)`. The prefix-sum bases are still computed when a side is empty; they are not zero.
:::

    assert str(final) == "231"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-ascii-memo
def ascii_memo(a, b):
    memo = {}

    def f(i, j):
        if (i, j) not in memo:
            if i == 0:
                memo[i, j] = sum(ord(b[k]) for k in range(j))
            elif j == 0:
                memo[i, j] = sum(ord(a[k]) for k in range(i))
            elif a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                memo[i, j] = f(i - 1, j - 1)
            else:
                memo[i, j] = min(f(i - 1, j) + ord(a[i - 1]), f(i, j - 1) + ord(b[j - 1]))
        return memo[i, j]

    return f(len(a), len(b))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int asciiMemo(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b, vector<vector<int>>& memo) {
    if (memo[i][j] >= 0) return memo[i][j];
    if (i == 0) { int s = 0; for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) s += b[k]; return memo[i][j] = s; }
    if (j == 0) { int s = 0; for (int k = 0; k < i; ++k) s += a[k]; return memo[i][j] = s; }
    if (a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]) return memo[i][j] = asciiMemo(i - 1, j - 1, a, b, memo);
    return memo[i][j] = min(asciiMemo(i - 1, j, a, b, memo) + a[i - 1], asciiMemo(i, j - 1, a, b, memo) + b[j - 1]);
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
The borders are prefix sums. Inside the grid a match copies the diagonal, and a mismatch pays the cheaper of the two deletions. The corner is the cost.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-ascii-tab
def ascii_tab(a, b):
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        dp[i][0] = dp[i - 1][0] + ord(a[i - 1])
    for j in range(1, m + 1):
        dp[0][j] = dp[0][j - 1] + ord(b[j - 1])
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1]
            else:
                dp[i][j] = min(dp[i - 1][j] + ord(a[i - 1]), dp[i][j - 1] + ord(b[j - 1]))
    return dp[n][m]
```

##### C++

```cpp
int asciiTab(const string& a, const string& b) {
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    vector<vector<int>> dp(n + 1, vector<int>(m + 1));
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) dp[i][0] = dp[i - 1][0] + a[i - 1];
    for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) dp[0][j] = dp[0][j - 1] + b[j - 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j)
            dp[i][j] = a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] ? dp[i - 1][j - 1]
                : min(dp[i - 1][j] + a[i - 1], dp[i][j - 1] + b[j - 1]);
    return dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

#### Heaviest common subsequence

::: {.form-next}
Put the letter's code on the LCS diagonal instead of `+ 1`, and take a maximum. Every kept letter is not paid on either string, so the delete cost is the sum of both strings minus twice that weight. On `sea` / `eat` the heaviest common subsequence is `ea` (198), the two strings sum to 627, and $627 - 396 = 231$.
:::

```{python}

    assert str(final) == "231"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-ascii-wt
def ascii_weight(a, b):
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + ord(a[i - 1])
            else:
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])
    total = sum(ord(ch) for ch in a) + sum(ord(ch) for ch in b)
    return total - 2 * dp[n][m]

assert ascii_rec("sea", "eat") == ascii_memo("sea", "eat") == ascii_tab("sea", "eat") == 231
assert ascii_weight("sea", "eat") == 231
assert ascii_tab("delete", "leet") == ascii_weight("delete", "leet") == 403
```

##### C++

```cpp
int asciiWeight(const string& a, const string& b) {
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    vector<vector<int>> dp(n + 1, vector<int>(m + 1));
    int total = 0;
    for (char ch : a) total += ch;
    for (char ch : b) total += ch;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j)
            dp[i][j] = a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] ? dp[i - 1][j - 1] + a[i - 1] : max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);
    return total - 2 * dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
Every form is $O(nm)$ after the borders. The recursion is only for the short samples; memoisation is the same bound as the table. Codes are at most 122 and lengths at most 1000, so the cost fits in a 32-bit integer. The weight form does the same arithmetic.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- One string empty: pay every code of the other.
- Equal strings: the cost is 0. The diagonal copies zero all the way.
- Two LCS of the same length can have different weights. `delete` / `leet` keeps `let`, not `eet`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- A zero border. In an LCS the empty prefix matches nothing and scores 0. Here the empty prefix is paid for in full. Sample 1 becomes wrong as soon as column 0 is left at 0.
- Keeping a longest common subsequence instead of a heaviest one. Length 3 is both `eet` and `let`. Only `let` costs 403.
- Forgetting the factor two in the weight form. A kept letter is saved in both strings.
:::

**Variants.** The same weighted diagonal with a third string is still a grid, one dimension larger. A score of $4 \cdot \mathrm{LCS} - |C| - |D|$ over substrings $C$ and $D$, rather than the whole strings, resets when a match is not worth keeping: [CF 1446B · Catching Cheaters](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1446/B){rating="1800"}.
